details:
**Joe Manchin**
West Virginia's longtime Democratic senator (2010–2025) and former governor, a centrist who often decided the outcome of votes in a closely divided Senate. He was the only Democrat to vote to confirm Supreme Court Justice Brett Kavanaugh in 2018.

**Jim Justice**
West Virginia's billionaire coal-and-resort owner who served as governor from 2017 to 2025 and then moved to the U.S. Senate. He was elected as a Democrat but switched to the Republican Party in 2017.

**Babydog**
Jim Justice's English bulldog, which he constantly brought to public events and used as a personal mascot, including in promoting the state's COVID-19 vaccine lottery.

**Build Back Better and Enersystems**
Joe Manchin's opposition helped sink Joe Biden's Build Back Better spending bill. Critics accused him of protecting his financial interests in Enersystems, a coal brokerage company founded by Manchin that is now run by his son.

**Patrick Morrisey**
West Virginia's Republican attorney general, who narrowly lost the 2018 Senate race to Joe Manchin. He was later elected governor and succeeded Jim Justice in 2025.

**Don Blankenship and "Cocaine Mitch"**
The former CEO of Massey Energy who served a year in prison for mine safety violations connected to the 2010 Upper Big Branch mine disaster. He ran unsuccessfully in the 2018 Republican Senate primary, airing ads attacking Mitch McConnell as "Cocaine Mitch."

**Richard Ojeda**
A populist Democratic state senator and Army veteran who supported the 2018 teachers' strike. He became the first candidate to drop out of the 2020 Democratic presidential primary.

**2018 teachers' strike**
A statewide strike by West Virginia public school teachers over low pay and health insurance costs. It won a raise and inspired similar teacher walkouts in other states.

**Supreme Court impeachments**
In August 2018, the West Virginia House of Delegates impeached all four sitting justices of the state Supreme Court of Appeals. The scandal involved lavish spending, including expensive office renovations.

**"Dead Aim" ad**
During the 2010 special election for the late Robert Byrd's Senate seat, Joe Manchin ran an ad in which he shot a copy of the cap-and-trade climate bill with a rifle.

**Robert Byrd**
West Virginia's Democratic senator from 1959 until his death in 2010, the longest-serving senator in U.S. history up to that time. His death led to the special election that Joe Manchin won.

**Carte Goodwin**
The man appointed in 2010 to briefly hold Robert Byrd's Senate seat until the special election. He was one of the youngest senators of his time and is known as the youngest living former senator.

**Gordon Gee and West Virginia University**
Gordon Gee, president of West Virginia University (the state's flagship school), oversaw a 2023 plan to cut many academic programs, including all of its world language majors, in order to close a budget deficit.

**Charleston**
The capital of West Virginia, an Appalachian state whose economy and politics have long been tied to coal mining.
